Independent Meeus computation gives 73.7% illuminated at that instant, and the app's own Dashboard Moon card says 'Waning Gibbous 74% illuminated' - so 74% is what the app itself computes and 100% is the renderer's. Chain confirmed in code: astronomy_calculations.dart:844-868 moonIllumination returns (1+cos)/2*100 i.e. a PERCENT; interactive_sky_view.dart:1026 passes `moonIllumination.illumination` as the third tuple slot; solar_system_and_markers.dart:484-486 does rawIllumination.clamp(0.0,1.0) and :571 does (illumination*100).round(). Any illumination above 1% pins to 1.0 -> 'MOON 100%' and a full terminator.

title: Mouse-wheel zoom discards ~99% of scroll events - 172 notches move the FOV from 60 to 29 degrees
reasoning: Reproduced and measured myself on the rebuilt bundle. 20 xdotool wheel-up notches at 50 ms spacing over the sky canvas moved FOV from 60.0 to exactly 50.0 - that is 60/1.2, the effect of ONE notch out of twenty (95% discarded). Then 5 notches at 2.0 s spacing moved 50.0 -> 21.9, which is exactly the compounded 50/1.2^3 then /1.15^2 = 21.88, i.e. every slow notch applies in full. Code confirms the mechanism at the cited line: interactive_sky_view.dart:475 `void _animateZoom(double newFOV)` reads _startFOV from the provider's CURRENT (barely-moved) fieldOfView and calls _zoomController.forward(from: 0.0) (:484) on every scroll event (:660-668), so a new notch restarts the 300 ms easeOutCubic from wherever the last one had crawled to instead of compounding onto the pending target. Location interactive_sky_view.dart:475 is exact. NOTE one sub-claim inside this finding is now false: the '=' and '-' hotkeys are NOT dead (see the focus finding) - keyboard zoom is a working alternative, which is why I leave this at P2 rather than raising it.

title: Alt/az readouts ignore precession - stated positions are up to 1.4 degrees off
reasoning: Reproduced with my own numbers. Clicked Vega at 2026-08-03 20:49:14 UTC from 40N/105W/1650m: popup reports RA 18h36m56.8s, Dec +38 47' 09" (J2000 to the arcsecond) and Current Position Alt 6.2 / Az 43.0. I computed alt/az from those unprecessed J2000 coordinates: 6.2436 / 43.0466 - an exact match. Precessing to the equinox of date (rigorous IAU 1976) gives RA 18h37m50s / +38 48' 36", whose alt/az is 6.1449 / 42.9005 - which the app does NOT show. No refraction either: at alt 6.2 deg refraction is ~0.13 deg and the app shows the bare geometric value. Corroborating code fact: AstronomyCalculations.precessFromJ2000ToDate exists at astronomy_calculations.dart:442 but a repo-wide grep finds ZERO call sites - it is dead code.
location_wrong: Cited only 'packages/skotiq_planetarium (horizontal transform)'. Precise sites for a fixer: the transform is AstronomyCalculations.equatorialToHorizontal at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:262, and the unused precession routine it should be composed with is precessFromJ2000ToDate at the same file :442.

title: Planets are computed for the equinox of date but stars and DSOs are drawn at J2000 - the two are mixed on one chart, so planets sit ~22 arcmin off the star background
reasoning: Reproduced with an independent ephemeris. Clicked Saturn at 2026-08-03 20:51:39 UTC: app reports RA 0h58m00.4s, Dec +3 26' 07". My own Keplerian ephemeris (JPL approximate elements, light-time corrected) gives J2000 geocentric 0h56m56.9s / +3 19' 59" and equinox-of-date 0h58m19.2s / +3 28' 35". The app sits 4.7 arcmin from the of-date value and 20 arcmin from J2000 - unambiguously equinox of date (the residual is within the app's truncated-VSOP and my Keplerian error budget for Saturn). In the same session Vega read out as its exact J2000 position (18h36m56.8s / +38 47' 09"). So the two families genuinely live in different frames on one chart; the offset at Saturn is 82s of RA plus 8.6 arcmin of Dec, ~22 arcmin total, matching the claim. Code confirms: planetary_positions.dart:145-153 converts VSOP-of-date ecliptic coordinates using the obliquity OF DATE, while the star catalogue is served J2000 and precessFromJ2000ToDate is never called.
location_wrong: Cited packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart. The planet frame is set in a DIFFERENT file: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/planetary_positions.dart:145-153 (`final obliquity = _obliquityJ2000 - 0.0130042 * tCenturies;` then eclipticToEquatorial). astronomy_calculations.dart is only relevant as the home of the unused precessFromJ2000ToDate (:442).

title: 'Best Targets Tonight' transit times are computed for the night after tomorrow - every time is ~8 minutes wrong
reasoning: The day-slip is real and I reproduced it deliberately, but the stated magnitude is wrong. Code is unchanged: mosaic_targets.dart:145-149 passes `imagingTime = twilight.astronomicalDusk` as the visibility `date`, and astronomy_calculations.dart:1106-1107 builds the search window as `DateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, 12)` + 24 h - so whenever dusk lands after local midnight the window is the NEXT night. On today's date (2026-08-03) astro dusk shows 23:58, still calendar day Aug 3, and the list's numbers are CORRECT: IC311 09:24 and NGC6685 00:48 match my own transit computation for the Aug-3-noon window (13:24:15 UTC and 04:48:52 UTC = 09:24 and 00:48 local). I then set the planetarium's date to Aug 2, 2026: astro dusk moves to 00:00 (calendar day Aug 3) and Best Targets STILL reports IC311 09:24 / NGC6685 00:48, whereas the correct values for the night of Aug 2 (Aug-2-noon window) are 09:28 and 00:52 by my computation. That is the bug, reproduced. CORRECTION TO THE FINDING: the slip is ONE night, ~4 minutes, not 'the night after tomorrow' / '~8 minutes'. Severity lowered to P3 accordingly - a 4-minute transit error does not change which target you pick, and the app is only wrong on the nights where dusk crosses midnight.
location_wrong: mosaic_targets.dart:146 is right for the caller. The other half a fixer must see is packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:1106-1107 (the localNoon/+24h window).
